newsitem.title: HUNGARY: RADICAL HUNGARY CPI CUT WOULD HARM GDP-THINK-TANK.
newsitem.headline: RADICAL HUNGARY CPI CUT WOULD HARM GDP-THINK-TANK.

text.p: The Hungarian government should approve the less radical of two alternative anti-inflation plans for 1998 on Thursday to avoid slowing economic growth, the think-tank Penzugykutato Rt said on Wednesday.

The government is to consider at its regular Thursday between two programmes, one aimed at an inflation cut to slightly below 10 percent in year-on-year terms for December 1998, and the other targeting levels of about 13 percent.
Hungary's inflation was running at 18.6 percent in April and the government forecast about 17 percent for December.
"We don't agree with the strained reduction to below 10 percent," analyst Zita Maria Petschnig told a news conference, adding that a radical cut would damage economic growth.
Hungary's gross domestic growth (GDP) target for 1997 is two to three percent, up from some one percent last year, and is forecast to rise to four to five percent for the years following 1997.
Petschnig added that even the moderate inflation plan would be a success.
"A three to four percentage point cut is realistic, and would be a good result."
Petschnig's recommendations tie in with recent comments by Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy which suggested the government was likely to adopt the less harsh of the two alternative strategies.
He said the government should approve an anti-inflation plan which would not harm economic growth.
Government bond dealers also said on Wednesday that the government was likely to approve the moderate inflation cut plan.
